import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Simple model that performs a single matrix multiplication (C = A * B) with a large K dimension
    """
    def __init__(self):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
    
    def forward(self, A: torch.Tensor, B: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Performs matrix multiplication of A and B.

        Args:
            A: Input tensor of shape (M, K)
            B: Input tensor of shape (K, N)

        Returns:
            Output tensor of shape (M, N)
        """
        return torch.matmul(A, B)

M = 256
N = 256
K = 131072 * 4

def get_inputs():
    A = torch.rand(M, K)
    B = torch.rand(K, N)
    return [A, B]

def get_init_inputs():
    return []  # No special initialization inputs needed

fix:
<reasoning>
The ptxas error "Unknown video selector: '.x'" at lines 31-32 of the PTX is caused by the declaration `.reg .b32 %tx, %ty, %tid, %bx, %by, %bz;` on line 20. `%tid` is a predefined PTX special register (`%tid.x`, `%tid.y`, `%tid.z`). Declaring a user register named `%tid` shadows it, so `mov.u32 %tx, %tid.x;` and `mov.u32 %ty, %tid.y;` parse `.x`/`.y` as illegal video selectors on a plain `.b32` register.

The minimal fix that preserves all kernel logic is to rename the user register `%tid` to `%lid` (linear thread id) in its declaration (line 20) and all its uses (lines 43, 44, 46, 47, 50, 51). The special-register reads on lines 35-36 remain unchanged and will now correctly resolve to the built-in `%tid.x`/`%tid.y`. I also update the comment on line 42 for consistency. Nothing else in the PTX or Python glue changes.
</reasoning>
